subject: Modular -> Tier harmonization options for Orthomed
messages:
From: Claire Barnes <claire@orthomed.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-01T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Exploring packaging options for our model usage

Hi Hannah,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Orthomed is excited about the potential to offload inference for our chart-summarization feature onto Redwood. Before we move to legal, procurement asked me to get clarity on two things:

- If we start on a modular (feature-by-feature) plan, how easy is it to move to a tiered seat/throughput plan later? Any pricing/proration implications?
- We need to understand bundling — e.g., if we take the Summarization + Protected-PHI routing add-on, is there a recommended bundle that gives cost predictability without overcommitting?

I've attached a quick spreadsheet with our projected monthly token usage and a few scenarios. Can Ben or someone on pricing send a recommended map and an example amendment they would expect at renewal?

Appreciate the help,
Claire
Claire Barnes
Head of Product Ops | Orthomed
Attachments: Orthomed_MA_Plan_Scenarios.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
To: Claire Barnes <claire@orthomed.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-01T12:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Exploring packaging options for our model usage

Claire — thanks for the spreadsheet. Looping in Ben (pricing) and Priya (CS) to propose a clear crosswalk. Quick notes before they dig in:

- Moving from modular to tiered is supported; we typically offer a 1-month proration on committed tiers during the first 90 days, then standard renewal rules after the first term.
- For Summarization + PHI routing we often recommend the "Core+Secure" bundle (documented below) to balance unit economics and compliance overhead.

Ben / Priya — can you review the attachment and propose 2 conservative paths (conservative-tier and aggressive-tier) plus any onboarding credits we can apply for the initial pilot?

Thanks,
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Director, Sales Operations | Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>, Claire Barnes <claire@orthomed.com>
Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-03T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Exploring packaging options for our model usage

Claire / team — attached is an offer summary and two suggested pathways based on your projected usage: conservative-tier (monthly commit ~120M tokens) and throughput-tier (monthly commit ~350M tokens with burst allowance). See highlights: 

- Conservative-tier: lower commit, higher per-token overage. Recommended for teams who want to move quickly and avoid long commitments. We can provide a 10% pilot discount for the first 3 months and 50k onboarding credits.
- Throughput-tier: committed throughput with a 12-month commitment. We can include automatic prefix-KV caching and a 1-month free capacity bump during launch (non-stackable). Pricing shown in Redwood_Offer_Summary_v3.pdf.

On modular -> tier migration: contract amendment is simple — we pro-rate the remainder of current month based on unused committed tokens and apply a one-time credit. For renewals, we lock at the negotiated tier pricing. I'll flag this internally as standard practice.

Questions for Claire: do you have an internal preference for commit length (3, 6, 12 months)? Also, Procurement asked about an example step-down policy for usage drops — we typically allow a one-step downgrade mid-term with a 30% fee on the price difference unless pre-negotiated.

Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Attachments: Redwood_Offer_Summary_v3.pdf

From: Claire Barnes <claire@orthomed.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
Cc: Orthomed Procurement <procurement@orthomed.com>
Date: 2028-06-04T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Exploring packaging options for our model usage

Thanks Ben — helpful. A couple follow-ups from procurement and finance: 

1) Step-down fee sounds high for us. If we commit 12 months but need to reduce capacity after month 6, can we propose a smaller step-down (e.g., 10-15%) tied to an expansion clause if we exceed the original commit later in the term?
2) For the throughput-tier, can onboarding credits be re-purposable toward usage overages instead of engineering credits? That helps our cost model.

We prefer a 12-month commit if the step-down is gentler. Also, will the KV caching and prefix cache be automatically enabled on throughput tiers? We want to understand if enabling caching requires configuration work from our side.

Claire
On Wed, Jun 3, 2028 at 09:18 AM Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com> wrote:
> Claire / team — attached is an offer summary and two suggested pathways based on your projected usage...

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-06T15:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Exploring packaging options for our model usage

Looping in as Hannah flagged. Ben — Claire's request about a gentler step-down is reasonable for strategic accounts. I approve offering the following concession for Orthomed (one-time exception):

- 12-month commit on throughput-tier with a 1-time downgrade option at month 6 with a 12% step-down fee (applies to price delta only).
- Onboarding credits: convert up to 50% of engineering onboarding credits to usage credits for the first 6 months.
- KV/prefix caching: enabled by default on throughput-tier; CS will coordinate a short config call to validate routing rules.

Please log the concession in the deal record and ensure legal adds an explicit fallback clause for step-downs. Priya, please prepare the short config runbook and a SOW addendum for enablement.

Marcus Lin
Sales Director | Redwood Inference

From: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
To: Claire Barnes <claire@orthomed.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
Cc: Orthomed Procurement <procurement@orthomed.com>
Date: 2028-06-08T16:44:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Exploring packaging options for our model usage - Next steps and docs

Claire — thanks, all. Confirming the plan and next steps: 

- Agreed commercial path: Throughput-tier, 12-month commit, with the one-time 12% step-down at month 6 as approved by Marcus.
- Credits: 50k onboarding credits, 50% convertible to usage credits for first 6 months.
- Technical: KV/prefix caching auto-enabled. I'll schedule a 60-min enablement call in the next week to validate routing and PHI-safe tagging.
- Docs: Ben attached the offer summary; I've uploaded the short enablement SOW we will append to the contract. Procurement: please review the DocuSign link and let us know if you need a redline.

Next actions for Orthomed: confirm acceptance of the 12% step-down concession and any redlines to the SOW.

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
Attachments: Redwood_Onboarding_SOW_v1.docx (SOW)
